items.stem: What is the lowest value of x² + 4x + 2?
items.answer:
x² + 4x + 2 = (x² + 4x + 4) − 2 = (x + 2)² − 2.
Here (x + 2)² is always non-negative and its lowest value is zero. Thus the lowest value of (x + 2)² − 2 is −2, attained when x + 2 = 0, i.e. x = −2.

items.stem: Calculate the zeroes of the polynomial p(x) = 4x² − 12x + 9.

Substituting p(x) = 0 and solving we get x = 3/2, 3/2.

items.stem: Find the values of a and b, if they are the zeroes of polynomial x² + ax + b.

items.stem: What are the zeroes of the polynomial x² − 3x − m(m + 3)?
items.answer:
p(x) = x² − 3x − m(m + 3).
Substituting x = −m: p(−m) = (−m)² − 3(−m) − m(m + 3) = m² + 3m − m² − 3m = 0, so x = −m is a zero.
Substituting x = m + 3: p(m + 3) = (m + 3)² − 3(m + 3) − m(m + 3) = (m + 3)[m + 3 − 3 − m] = (m + 3)(0) = 0, so x = m + 3 is also a zero.
Hence the zeroes are −m and m + 3.

items.stem: Find the value of k such that the polynomial x² − (k + 6)x + 2(2k + 1) has sum of its zeroes equal to half of their product.

items.stem: If the zeroes of the polynomial x² + px + q are double in value to the zeroes of 2x² − 5x − 3, find the value of p and q.
items.answer: We have f(x) = 2x² − 5x − 3. Let its zeroes be α and β, then sum of zeroes α + β = 5/2 and product of zeroes αβ = −3/2. items.stem: Find a quadratic polynomial whose zeroes are reciprocals of the zeroes of the polynomial f(x) = ax² + bx + c, a ≠ 0, c ≠ 0.
items.answer: Let α and β be the zeroes of ax² + bx + c, so α + β = −b/a and αβ = c/a. Let 1/α and 1/β be the zeroes of the new polynomial. Sum of zeroes, s = 1/α + 1/β = (β + α)/(αβ) = (−b/a)/(c/a) = −b/c. Product of zeroes, p = 1/α × 1/β = 1/(αβ) = a/c. Required polynomial g(x) = x² − sx + p = x² + (b/c)x + a/c, i.e. c·g(x) = cx² + bx + a. Hence g(x) = cx² + bx + a.
items.concept: Sum and product of the zeroes

items.stem: If the sum and product of the zeroes of the polynomial ax² − 5x + c are equal to 10 each, find the value of "a" and "c".

items.stem: If one zero of the polynomial 3x² − 8x + 2k + 1 is seven times the other, find the value of k.

items.stem: Find the quadratic polynomial, the sum and product of whose zeroes are −3 and 2 respectively. Hence find the zeroes.

items.stem: Find the zeroes of the quadratic polynomial 6x² − 3 − 7x and verify the relationship between the zeroes and the coefficients.
items.answer: For zeroes, p(x) = 0: 6x² − 7x − 3 = 0 ⇒ 6x² − 9x + 2x − 3 = 0 ⇒ 3x(2x − 3) + 1(2x − 3) = 0 ⇒ (2x − 3)(3x + 1) = 0. Thus x = 3/2 and x = −1/3, so α = 3/2 and β = −1/3 are the zeroes. Verification: α + β = 3/2 + (−1/3) = 7/6 = −(coefficient of x)/(coefficient of x²) = −(−7)/6. Product αβ = (3/2)(−1/3) = −1/2 = (constant term)/(coefficient of x²) = −3/6.

items.stem: Find the zeroes of the quadratic polynomial x² + 7x + 10 and verify the relationship between the zeroes and the coefficients.

Adding (1) and (2) gives 5a = 0 ⇒ a = 0. Substituting a = 0 in (1) gives b = −6. Hence a = 0 and b = −6.

items.stem: If α and β are the zeroes of the polynomial 6y² − 7y + 2, find a quadratic polynomial whose zeroes are 1/α and 1/β.

For the new polynomial g(y): sum of zeroes = 1/α + 1/β = (α + β)/(αβ) = (7/6)/(2/6) = 7/2, and product of zeroes = 1/α × 1/β = 1/(αβ) = 1/(1/3) = 3. Hence g(y) = y² − (7/2)y + 3 = ½(2y² − 7y + 6).

items.stem: Find the zeroes of the quadratic polynomial 5x² + 8x − 4 and verify the relationship between the zeroes and the coefficients of the polynomial.
items.answer: p(x) = 5x² + 8x − 4 = 5x² + 10x − 2x − 4 = 5x(x + 2) − 2(x + 2) = (x + 2)(5x − 2). Substituting p(x) = 0 gives the zeroes −2 and 2/5. Verification: sum of zeroes = −2 + 2/5 = −8/5, and from the polynomial −b/a = −(coefficient of x)/(coefficient of x²) = −8/5. Product of zeroes = (−2)(2/5) = −4/5, and c/a = (constant term)/(coefficient of x²) = −4/5. Hence verified.

items.stem: Find the zeroes of the quadratic polynomial x² − 2√2x and verify the relationship between the zeroes and the coefficients of the polynomial.
items.answer: x² − 2√2x = x(x − 2√2). Setting p(x) = 0 gives x = 0 and x = 2√2, so the zeroes are 0 and 2√2. Verification: sum of zeroes = 0 + 2√2 = 2√2 = −(coefficient of x)/(coefficient of x²) = −(−2√2)/1. Product of zeroes = 0 × 2√2 = 0 = (constant term)/(coefficient of x²) = 0/1. Hence verified.

items.stem: If α and β are the zeroes of a quadratic polynomial such that α + β = 24 and α − β = 8, find the quadratic polynomial having α and β as its zeroes.
items.answer: We have α + β = 24 …(1) and α − β = 8 …(2). Adding (1) and (2): 2α = 32 ⇒ α = 16. Subtracting (2) from (1): 2β = 16 ⇒ β = 8. Hence the quadratic polynomial is p(x) = x² − (α + β)x + αβ = x² − (16 + 8)x + (16)(8) = x² − 24x + 128.
items.concept: Sum and product of the zeroes

items.stem: When p(x) = x² + 7x + 9 is divided by g(x), we get (x + 2) and −1 as the quotient and remainder respectively, find g(x).
items.answer: Here p(x) = x² + 7x + 9, q(x) = x + 2 and r(x) = −1. By the division algorithm p(x) = g(x)·q(x) + r(x), so x² + 7x + 9 = g(x)(x + 2) − 1. Hence g(x) = (x² + 7x + 10)/(x + 2) = (x + 2)(x + 5)/(x + 2) = x + 5. Thus g(x) = x + 5.

items.stem: Find the value for k for which x⁴ + 10x³ + 25x² + 15x + k is exactly divisible by x + 7.
items.answer: Let f(x) = x⁴ + 10x³ + 25x² + 15x + k. If x + 7 is a factor then −7 is a zero of f(x), so x = −7 satisfies f(x) = 0. Substituting x = −7: (−7)⁴ + 10(−7)³ + 25(−7)² + 15(−7) + k = 0 ⇒ 2401 − 3430 + 1225 − 105 + k = 0 ⇒ 3626 − 3535 + k = 0 ⇒ 91 + k = 0 ⇒ k = −91.

items.stem: On dividing the polynomial 4x⁴ − 5x³ − 39x² − 46x − 2 by the polynomial g(x) the quotient is x² − 3x − 5 and the remainder is −5x + 8. Find the polynomial g(x).
items.answer: Dividend = (Divisor × Quotient) + Remainder, so 4x⁴ − 5x³ − 39x² − 46x − 2 = g(x)(x² − 3x − 5) + (−5x + 8). Therefore 4x⁴ − 5x³ − 39x² − 46x − 2 + 5x − 8 = g(x)(x² − 3x − 5), i.e. 4x⁴ − 5x³ − 39x² − 41x − 10 = g(x)(x² − 3x − 5). Hence g(x) = (4x⁴ − 5x³ − 39x² − 41x − 10)/(x² − 3x − 5) = 4x² + 7x + 2.

items.stem: If the squared difference of the zeroes of the quadratic polynomial f(x) = x² + px + 45 is equal to 144, find the value of p.
items.answer: Let α and β be the zeroes of f(x) = x² + px + 45. Sum of zeroes α + β = −p and product of zeroes αβ = 45. Given (α − β)² = 144, i.e. (α + β)² − 4αβ = 144. Substituting the values: (−p)² − 4 × 45 = 144 ⇒ p² − 180 = 144 ⇒ p² = 144 + 180 = 324 ⇒ p = ±√324 = ±18. Hence the value of p is ±18.
items.concept: Sum and product of the zeroes

items.stem: Polynomial x⁴ + 7x³ + 7x² + px + q is exactly divisible by x² + 7x + 12, then find the value of p and q.
items.answer: x² + 7x + 12 = 0 ⟹ x² + 4x + 3x + 12 = 0 ⟹ x(x + 4) + 3(x + 4) = 0 ⟹ (x + 4)(x + 3) = 0, so x = −4 and x = −3. Since f(x) = x⁴ + 7x³ + 7x² + px + q is exactly divisible by x² + 7x + 12, both x = −4 and x = −3 must be zeroes of f(x) and must satisfy f(x) = 0. f(−4): 256 − 448 + 112 − 4p + q = 0 ⟹ 4p − q = −80 ...(1). f(−3): 81 − 189 + 63 − 3p + q = 0 ⟹ 3p − q = −45 ...(2). Subtracting (2) from (1): p = −35. Substituting in (1): 4(−35) − q = −80 ⟹ −q = 60 ⟹ q = −60. Hence p = −35 and q = −60.

items.stem: If α and β are the zeroes of the polynomial p(x) = 2x² + 5x + k satisfying the relation α² + β² + αβ = 21/4, then find the value of k.
items.answer: For p(x) = 2x² + 5x + k, sum of zeroes α + β = −b/a = −5/2 and product of zeroes αβ = c/a = k/2. Now α² + β² + αβ = (α² + β² + 2αβ) − αβ = (α + β)² − αβ = 21/4. Substituting, (−5/2)² − k/2 = 21/4 ⟹ k/2 = 25/4 − 21/4 = 4/4 = 1. Hence k = 2.

items.stem: Find the zeroes of the quadratic polynomial 7y² − (11/3)y − 2/3 and verify the relationship between the zeroes and the coefficients.
items.answer: 7y² − (11/3)y − 2/3 = 0 ⟹ 21y² − 11y − 2 = 0 ⟹ 21y² − 14y + 3y − 2 = 0 ⟹ 7y(3y − 2) + (3y − 2) = 0 ⟹ (3y − 2)(7y + 1) = 0. Hence the zeroes are y = 2/3 and y = −1/7. Comparing 21y² − 11y − 2 with ay² + by + c, a = 21, b = −11, c = −2. Sum of roots α + β = 2/3 + (−1/7) = 2/3 − 1/7 = 11/21 = −b/a, hence verified. Product of roots αβ = (2/3) × (−1/7) = −2/21 = c/a, hence verified.
items.concept: Sum and product of the zeroes

items.stem: If α and β are the zeroes of polynomial p(x) = 3x² + 2x + 1, find the polynomial whose zeroes are (1 − α)/(1 + α) and (1 − β)/(1 + β).
items.answer: For p(x) = 3x² + 2x + 1, α + β = −2/3 and αβ = 1/3. Let α₁ and β₁ be the zeroes of the new polynomial q(x). Sum of zeroes: α₁ + β₁ = (1 − α)/(1 + α) + (1 − β)/(1 + β) = [(1 − α + β − αβ) + (1 + α − β − αβ)]/[(1 + α)(1 + β)] = (2 − 2αβ)/(1 + α + β + αβ) = (2 − 2/3)/(1 − 2/3 + 1/3) = (4/3)/(2/3) = 2. Product of zeroes: α₁β₁ = (1 − α)(1 − β)/[(1 + α)(1 + β)] = [1 − (α + β) + αβ]/[1 + (α + β) + αβ] = (1 + 2/3 + 1/3)/(1 − 2/3 + 1/3) = 2/(2/3) = 3. Hence the required polynomial is q(x) = x² − (α₁ + β₁)x + α₁β₁ = x² − 2x + 3.
items.concept: Sum and product of the zeroes

items.stem: If α and β are the zeroes of the polynomial x² + 4x + 3, find the polynomial whose zeroes are 1 + β/α and 1 + α/β.
items.answer: For x² + 4x + 3, α + β = −4 and αβ = 3. The new zeroes are 1 + β/α = (α + β)/α and 1 + α/β = (α + β)/β. Sum = (α + β)(1/α + 1/β) = (α + β)²/(αβ) = 16/3 and product = (α + β)²/(αβ) = 16/3. Hence the required polynomial is x² − (16/3)x + 16/3 = (1/3)(3x² − 16x + 16).

items.stem: Box : For the box to satisfy certain requirements, its length must be three unit greater than the width, and its height must be two unit less than the width. (i) If width is taken as x, find the polynomial that represent volume of box. (ii) Find the polynomial that represent the area of paper sheet used to make box. (iii) If it must have a volume of 18 unit, what must be its length and height? (iv) If box is made of a paper sheet which cost is Rs 100 per square unit, what is the cost of paper?
items.answer: (i) If x represents the width, the length is x + 3 and the height is x − 2. Volume V(x) = WLH = x(x + 3)(x − 2) = x(x² + x − 6) = x³ + x² − 6x. (ii) Surface area S(x) = 2(LW + WH + HL) = 2[x(x + 3) + (x + 3)(x − 2) + x(x − 2)] = 2[x² + 3x + x² + x − 6 + x² − 2x] = 2(3x² + 2x − 6) = 6x² + 4x − 12. (iii) 18 = x³ + x² − 6x ⟹ x³ + x² − 6x − 18 = 0. There is only one change of sign, so only one positive zero; substituting x = 3 gives 27 + 9 − 18 − 18 = 0, so the width is 3 unit, length = x + 3 = 6 unit and height = x − 2 = 1 unit. (iv) S(3) = 6(3)² + 4(3) − 12 = 54 square unit, so cost C = 100 × 54 = Rs 5400.
items.concept: Linear, quadratic and cubic

items.stem: Cubic Coating : Frozen specimens are stored in a cubic metal box that is x inches on each side. The box is surrounded by a 2 inch thick layer of foam insulation. (i) Find a polynomial function V(x) that gives the total volume in cubic inches for the box and insulation. (ii) Find the total volume if x is 10 inches. (iii) Use the remainder theorem to find the total volume when x is 10 inches.
items.answer: (i) Since 2 inches of foam is added all around the box, each side is now x + 4 inches. V(x) = (x + 4)³ = (x + 4)(x² + 8x + 16) = x³ + 12x² + 48x + 64. (ii) V(10) = 10³ + 12 × 10² + 48 × 10 + 64 = 1000 + 1200 + 480 + 64 = 2744 in³. (iii) Dividing V(x) = x³ + 12x² + 48x + 64 by x − 10 gives quotient x² + 22x + 268 and remainder 2744, so V(10) = 2744 in³.

items.stem: Swimming Pool : The volume of water in a rectangular, in-ground, swimming pool is given by V(x) = x³ + 11x² + 24x, where V(x) is the volume in cubic feet when the water is x ft high. (i) Find the dimension of base of pool. (ii) Use the remainder theorem to find the volume when x = 3 ft. (iii) If the volume is 100 ft³ of water, what is the height x? (iv) If the maximum capacity of the pool is 520 ft³, what is the maximum depth?
items.answer: (i) V(x) = x³ + 11x² + 24x = x(x² + 11x + 24) = x(x + 3)(x + 8). If x represents the height, the base dimensions are (x + 3) and (x + 8). (ii) Dividing V(x) = x³ + 11x² + 24x by x − 3 gives quotient x² + 14x + 66 and remainder 198, so V(3) = 198 ft³. (iii) 100 = x³ + 11x² + 24x ⟹ x³ + 11x² + 24x − 100 = 0. There is one change of sign, so only one positive solution; x = 2 divides it exactly (quotient x² + 13x + 50). Thus the height is 2 ft. (iv) 520 = x³ + 11x² + 24x ⟹ x³ + 11x² + 24x − 520 = 0; x = 5 divides it exactly (quotient x² + 16x + 104). Thus the maximum depth is 5 ft.

items.stem: Overflow Pan : A metalworker makes an overflow pan by cutting equal squares with sides of length x from the corners of a 30 cm by 20 cm piece of aluminium, as shown in the figure. The sides are then folded up and the corners sealed. (i) Find a polynomial function V(x) that gives the volume of the pan. (ii) Find the volume of the pan if the height is 6 cm. Use remainder theorem.
items.answer: (i) Since x is taken off both ends of each side, the base measures (20 − 2x) by (30 − 2x). V(x) = x(20 − 2x)(30 − 2x) = x(4x² − 100x + 600) = 4x³ − 100x² + 600x. (ii) Dividing V(x) = 4x³ − 100x² + 600x by x − 6 gives quotient 4x² − 76x + 144 and remainder 864. Hence the volume is 864 cm³ at x = 6 cm.
items.concept: Linear, quadratic and cubic

items.stem: Square Pan : Suppose that the pan in the previous question is formed from a square piece of aluminium that is 30 cm on each side. (i) Find a polynomial function V(x) that gives the volume in cubic cm. (ii) The cost is Rs 5 per square cm of aluminium used in the finished pan. Find a polynomial function C(x) that gives the cost.
items.answer: (i) Since x is taken off both ends of each side of the square, the base measures (30 − 2x) by (30 − 2x). V(x) = x(30 − 2x)(30 − 2x) = x(4x² − 120x + 900) = 4x³ − 120x² + 900x. (ii) The area of the bottom of the pan is (30 − 2x)(30 − 2x) = 4x² − 120x + 900 and the area of the 4 sides is 4(x)(30 − 2x) = 120x − 8x². Total area = −4x² + 900 square cm. Multiplying by Rs 5 per square cm, C(x) = −20x² + 4500, which gives the cost in rupees.

items.stem: Volume of a Bird Cage : A company makes rectangular shaped bird cages with height b inches and square bottoms. The volume of these cages is given by the function V = b³ − 6b² + 9b. (i) Find an expression for the length of each side of the square bottom. (ii) Use the function to find the volume of a cage with a height of 18 inches. (iii) Use the remainder theorem to find the volume of a cage with a height of 15 inches. (iv) Verify the result of (iii) using the function.
items.answer: (i) V = b³ − 6b² + 9b = b(b² − 6b + 9) = b(b − 3)(b − 3). If b is the height, then (b − 3) is the length of each side of the square bottom. (ii) V(18) = 18(18 − 3)(18 − 3) = 18 × 15 × 15 = 4050 in³. (iii) Dividing b³ − 6b² + 9b by b − 15 gives quotient b² + 9b + 144 and remainder 2160, so V(15) = 2160 in³. (iv) V(15) = 15(15 − 3)(15 − 3) = 15 × 12 × 12 = 2160 in³, which verifies the result of (iii).

items.stem: Propylene Storage Tank : R K Agrawal is designing a propylene tank in the shape of a cylinder with hemispherical ends. If the length of the cylinder is to be 20 unit larger than its radius and the volume is to be 3321π cubic unit, then what is the radius?
items.answer: Let x be the radius of the cylindrical part and of the hemispheres, since both are common. The volume of a hemisphere of radius x is (1/2)(4/3)πx³ and the volume of the cylinder of radius x and height x + 20 is πx²(x + 20). The tank consists of 2 hemispheres and one cylinder with total volume 3321π, so (4/3)πx³ + πx²(x + 20) = 3321π ⟹ 4x³ + 3x²(x + 20) = 9963 ⟹ 7x³ + 60x² − 9963 = 0. There is only one change of sign, so only one positive zero; by trial x = 9 divides it exactly (quotient 7x² + 123x + 1107). The radius is 9 unit.

items.stem: Cereal Box : An independent marketing research agency has determined that the best box for breakfast cereal has a height that is 6 inches larger than its thickness and a width that is 5 inches larger than its thickness. (i) If we let the thickness be x inches, find a polynomial function V(x) that gives the total volume. (ii) If such a box is to have a volume of 112 inches³, then what should the thickness be?
items.answer: (i) If the thickness is x inches, the height is x + 6 inches and the width is x + 5 inches. V(x) = x(x + 6)(x + 5) = x(x² + 11x + 30) = x³ + 11x² + 30x. (ii) 112 = x³ + 11x² + 30x ⟹ x³ + 11x² + 30x − 112 = 0. There is only one change of sign, so only one positive zero; x = 2 divides it exactly (quotient x² + 13x + 56). Thus the thickness should be 2 inch.

items.stem: A bulk dog food storage bin with dimensions 2 feet by 3 feet by 4 feet needs to be increased in size to hold five times as much food as the current bin. Assume each dimension is increased by the same amount. (i) Let x be the amount by which dimension is increased. Write a function that represents the volume of the new bin. (ii) Find the dimensions of the new bin.
items.answer: (i) If every dimension is increased by x, the new dimensions are x + 2, x + 3 and x + 4, so V(x) = (x + 2)(x + 3)(x + 4) = (x + 2)(x² + 7x + 12) = x³ + 9x² + 26x + 24. (ii) Original volume V = 2 × 3 × 4 = 24. The new volume must be 5 times this, so 24 × 5 = x³ + 9x² + 26x + 24 ⟹ x³ + 9x² + 26x − 96 = 0. There is only one change of sign, so only one positive solution; x = 2 divides it exactly (quotient x² + 11x + 48). Thus each dimension is increased by 2 feet and the new bin measures 4 feet, 5 feet and 6 feet.
items.concept: Linear, quadratic and cubic

items.stem: The discharge rate of a river is a measure of the river's water flow as it empties into a lake, sea, or ocean. The rate depends on many factors, but is primarily influenced by the precipitation in the surrounding area and is often seasonal. Suppose the discharge rate of the Brahmaputra River was modelled by D(m) = −m⁴ + 22m³ − 147m² + 317m + 150, where D(m) represents the discharge rate in thousands of cubic meters of water per second in month m (m = 1 Jan, m = 2 Feb, ...). (i) What was the discharge rate in June (summer heat)? (ii) Is the discharge rate higher in June or October?
items.answer: (i) To find the discharge rate in June we find D(6) by the remainder theorem, dividing −m⁴ + 22m³ − 147m² + 317m + 150 by m − 6. The quotient is −m³ + 16m² − 51m + 11 and the remainder is 216, so D(6) = 216 thousand cubic metres per second. (ii) Dividing the same polynomial by m − 10 gives quotient −m³ + 12m² − 27m + 47 and remainder 620, so D(10) = 620 thousand cubic metres per second. The discharge rate during the fall rains in October is much higher than in June.
items.concept: Degree of a polynomial
items.ocr: The printed text spells the river 'Brhamputra'; corrected to Brahmaputra. The second long division prints the dividend coefficient as −1447m²; restored to −147m² from the model.

items.stem: Cost of Production : The cost to produce bottled spring water is given by C(x) = 16x − 63, where x is the number of thousands of bottles. The total income (revenue) from the sale of these bottles is given by the function R(x) = −x² + 326x − 7463. (i) Since Profit = Revenue − Cost, find the profit function. (ii) How many bottles sold will produce the maximum profit? (iii) What is the maximum profit? (iv) Find the profit when 245 thousand bottles are sold. Use remainder theorem.
items.answer: (i) P(x) = R(x) − C(x) = (−x² + 326x − 7463) − (16x − 63) = −x² + 310x − 7400. (ii) Completing the square, P(x) = −(x² − 310x + 155²) + 155² − 7400 = −(x − 155)² + 16625, so P(x) is maximum at x = 155; for maximum profit 155 thousand bottles must be sold. (iii) The maximum profit is Rs 16625. (iv) Dividing P(x) = −x² + 310x − 7400 by x − 245 gives quotient −x + 65 and remainder 8525, so when 245 thousand bottles are sold the profit is Rs 8525.
items.concept: General form of a quadratic

items.stem: Selection of Bridesmaids : A bride-to-be has many girlfriends, but she has decided to have only five bridesmaids, including the maid of honour. The number of different ways n girlfriends can be chosen and assigned a position, such as maid of honour, first bridesmaid, second bridesmaid, and so on, is given by the polynomial function S(n) = n⁵ − 10n⁴ + 35n³ − 50n² + 8n. (i) Use the Remainder Theorem to determine the number of ways the bride can select her bridesmaids if she chooses from n = 5 girlfriends. (ii) Evaluate S(n) for n = 5 by substituting 5 for n. How does this result compare with the result obtained in (i)?
items.answer: (i) Dividing S(n) = n⁵ − 10n⁴ + 35n³ − 50n² + 8n by n − 5 gives quotient n⁴ − 5n³ + 10n² + 8 and remainder 40, so S(5) = 40. The bride can select her bridesmaids in 40 ways. (ii) S(5) = 5⁵ − 10 × 5⁴ + 35 × 5³ − 50 × 5² + 8 × 5 = 3125 − 6250 + 4375 − 1250 + 40 = 40, the same result as obtained in (i) by the Remainder Theorem.
items.concept: Degree of a polynomial

items.stem: Display of Soda Cans : The number of soda cans S needed to build a square pyramid display with n levels is given by the function L(n) = (1/3)n³ + (1/2)n² + (1/6)n. Use the Remainder Theorem to determine the number of soda cans needed to build a square pyramid display with n = 6 levels.
items.answer: To find L(6) using the remainder theorem we divide L(n) = (1/3)n³ + (1/2)n² + (1/6)n by n − 6. The quotient is (1/3)n² + (5/2)n + 91/6 and the remainder is 91. Hence L(6) = 91, so 91 soda cans are needed.

items.stem: Volume of Solid : A cuboidal solid of base x by x + 1 is shown in the figure. Height of original solid is x + 2. A small cuboidal solid of base x − 2 by x − 2 and height 2 is cut from this solid as shown in the figure. (i) Find the polynomial for the volume of remaining solid. (ii) Use the remainder theorem to determine the volume of remaining solid at x = 8 inch. (iii) Use the polynomial to determine the volume at x = 8 inch and verify the result in (ii). (iv) Use the remainder theorem to determine the volume at x = 10 inch.
items.answer: (i) Volume of the original solid Vo(x) = x(x + 1)(x + 2) = x(x² + 3x + 2) = x³ + 3x² + 2x. Volume of the solid cut away Vs(x) = 2(x − 2)(x − 2) = 2(x² − 4x + 4) = 2x² − 8x + 8. Volume of the remaining solid V(x) = Vo(x) − Vs(x) = x³ + 3x² + 2x − 2x² + 8x − 8 = x³ + x² + 10x − 8. (ii) Dividing V(x) = x³ + x² + 10x − 8 by x − 8 gives quotient x² + 9x + 82 and remainder 648, so V(8) = 648 cubic inch. (iii) V(8) = 8³ + 8² + 10 × 8 − 8 = 512 + 64 + 80 − 8 = 648 cubic inch, which verifies (ii). (iv) Dividing V(x) by x − 10 gives quotient x² + 11x + 120 and remainder 1192, so V(10) = 1192 cubic inch.
items.concept: Linear, quadratic and cubic

items.stem: The Prime Minister's Citizen Assistance and Relief in Emergency Situations Fund was created on 28 March 2020, following the COVID-19 pandemic in India. The fund will be used for combating, and containment and relief efforts against the coronavirus outbreak and similar pandemic like situations in the future. The allotment officer is trying to come up with a method to calculate fair division of funds across various affected families so that the fund amount and amount received per family can be easily adjusted based on daily revised numbers. The total fund allotted for a village is x³ + 6x² + 20x + 9. The officer has divided the fund equally among families of the village and each family receives an amount of x² + 2x + 2. After distribution, some amount is left. (i) How many families are there in the village? (ii) If an amount of Rs 1911 is left after distribution, what is value of x? (iii) How much amount does each family receive? (iv) What is the amount of fund allocated? (v) How many families are there in the village?
items.answer: (i) Dividing x³ + 6x² + 20x + 9 by x² + 2x + 2 gives quotient x + 4 and remainder 10x + 1. The number of families is (x + 4). (ii) Amount left = 10x + 1 = 1911 ⟹ x = 1910/10 = 191. (iii) Since x = 191, the amount received by each family is x² + 2x + 2 = 191² + 2(191) + 2 = 36865. (iv) Since x = 191, the allotted fund is x³ + 6x² + 20x + 9 = (x² + 2x + 2)(x + 4) + 10x + 1 = 36865(191 + 4) + 1911 = 71,90,586. (v) Number of families = x + 4 = 191 + 4 = 195.
items.concept: Linear, quadratic and cubic
items.ocr: Printed parts (i) and (v) ask the same question; kept as printed, with (i) answered as the polynomial (x + 4) and (v) numerically as 195. The rupee symbol in part (ii) OCRs as '¥1911 s eft'; restored to 'Rs 1911 is left'. The printed total for part (iv) reads 69,72,846, which is arithmetically wrong: both 36865 × 195 + 1911 and 191³ + 6(191)² + 20(191) + 9 give 71,90,586; corrected.

items.stem: Pyramid, in architecture, a monumental structure constructed of or faced with stone or brick and having a rectangular base and four sloping triangular sides meeting at an apex. Pyramids have been built at various times in Egypt, Sudan, Ethiopia, western Asia, Greece, Cyprus, Italy, India, Thailand, Mexico, South America, and on some islands of the Pacific Ocean. Those of Egypt and of Central and South America are the best known. The volume and surface area of a pyramid with a square base of area a² and height h is given by V = ha²/3 and S = a² + 2a√((a/2)² + h²). A pyramid has a square base and a volume of 3y³ + 18y² + 27y cubic units. (i) If its height is y, then what polynomial represents the length of a side of the square base? (ii) If area of base is 576 metre², what is the side of base? (iii) What is the height of pyramid at above area of base? (iv) What is the ratio of length of side to the height? (v) What is surface area of pyramid?
items.answer: V(y) = 3y³ + 18y² + 27y = 3y(y² + 6y + 9) = 3y(y + 3)². (i) If y is the height, comparing with the standard volume ya²/3 = 3y(y + 3)² gives a² = 9(y + 3)², so a = 3(y + 3). (ii) a² = 576 ⟹ a = 24 unit. (iii) 24 = 3(y + 3) ⟹ 8 = y + 3 ⟹ y = 5 metre. (iv) a/y = 24/5. (v) S = a² + 2a√((a/2)² + h²) = 24² + 2 × 24√(12² + 5²) = 2 × 24(12 + 13) = 48 × 25 = 1200 m².

items.stem: SBL Fabricators has got an order for making a frame for machine of their client. For which, they are using AutoCAD software to create a constructible model that includes the relevant information such as dimensions of the frame and materials needed. The frame will have a solid base and will be cut out of a piece of steel. The final area of the frame should be 54 sq m. The diagram of frame is shown below. In order to input the right values in the AutoCAD software, the engineer needs to calculate some basic values. (i) What are the dimensions of the outer frame? (ii) A metal sheet of minimum area is used to make the frame. What should be the minimum area of metal sheet before cutting? (iii) What is the area of required final metal frame? (iv) If the area of the frame is 54 sq m, what is the value of x? (v) What is the perimeter of the frame?
items.answer: (i) Length = (10 + x + x) = (10 + 2x) and breadth = (5 + x + x) = (5 + 2x). (ii) Area of the steel plate A = lb = (10 + 2x)(5 + 2x) = 50 + 10x + 20x + 4x² = 4x² + 30x + 50. (iii) Area of frame to be cut = 10 × 5 = 50 m², so area of frame left = 4x² + 30x + 50 − 50 = 4x² + 30x m². (iv) 4x² + 30x = 54 ⟹ 2x² + 15x − 27 = 0 ⟹ 2x² + 18x − 3x − 27 = 0 ⟹ (x + 9)(2x − 3) = 0 ⟹ x = 1.5 or x = −9; taking the positive value, x = 1.5 m. (v) Perimeter = perimeter of the outside rectangle = 2(10 + 2x + 5 + 2x) = 2(15 + 4x) = 2(15 + 4 × 1.5) = 42 m.

items.stem: A barrels manufacturer can produce up to 300 barrels per day. The profit made from the sale of these barrels can be modelled by the function P(x) = −10x² + 3500x − 66000, where P(x) is the profit in rupees and x is the number of barrels made and sold. Based on this model answer the following questions: (i) When no barrels are produced what is the profit/loss? (ii) What is the break even point? (Zero profit point is called break even) (iii) What is the profit/loss if 175 barrels are produced? (iv) What is the profit/loss if 400 barrels are produced? (v) What is the maximum profit which the manufacturer can earn?

items.stem: Lavanya throws a ball upwards, from a rooftop, which is 20 m above from ground. It will reach a maximum height and then fall back to the ground. The height of the ball from the ground at time t is h, which is given by h = −4t² + 16t + 20. (i) What is the height reached by the ball after 1 second? (ii) What is the maximum height reached by the ball? (iii) How long will the ball take to hit the ground? (iv) What are the two possible times to reach the ball at the same height of 32 m? (v) Where is the ball after 5 seconds?
items.answer: (i) At t = 1 second, h = −4(1)² + 16(1) + 20 = 32 m. (ii) Completing the square, h = −4(t² − 4t − 5) = −4[(t − 2)² − 9] = −4(t − 2)² + 36, so the height is maximum at t = 2 and h(max) = 36 m. (iii) When the ball hits the ground h = 0, so −4t² + 16t + 20 = 0 ⟹ t² − 4t − 5 = 0 ⟹ (t − 5)(t + 1) = 0, giving t = 5 or t = −1. Time cannot be negative, so t = 5 seconds. (iv) 32 = −4t² + 16t + 20 ⟹ t² − 4t + 3 = 0 ⟹ t² − 3t − t + 3 = 0 ⟹ (t − 1)(t − 3) = 0, so t = 1 s and t = 3 s. (v) From (iii), at t = 5 we have h = 0, so the ball hits the ground at 5 seconds and after that it rebounds.
items.concept: What a zero is

items.stem: Underground water tank is very popular in India. It is usually used for large water tank storage and can be built cheaply using cement-like materials. Underground water tanks are typically chosen by people who want to save space. The water in the underground water tank is not affected by extreme weather conditions. The underground water tank maintains cool temperatures in both winter and summer. A builder wants to build a tank to store water in an apartment. The volume of the rectangular tank will be modelled by V(x) = x³ + x² − 4x − 4. (i) He planned in such a way that its base dimensions are (x + 1) and (x + 2). How much he has to dig? (ii) If x = 4 metre, what is the volume of the water tank? (iii) If x = 4 and the builder wants to paint the entire inner portion on the water tank, what is the total area to be painted? (iv) If the cost of paint is Rs 25 per square metre, what is the cost of painting? (v) What is the storage capacity of this water tank?
items.answer: (i) V(x) = x³ + x² − 4x − 4 = x²(x + 1) − 4(x + 1) = (x + 1)(x² − 4) = (x + 1)(x − 2)(x + 2). If (x + 1) and (x + 2) are two dimensions, the third is (x − 2), so he has to dig (x − 2). (ii) V(4) = (4 + 1)(4 − 2)(4 + 2) = 5 × 2 × 6 = 60 m³. (iii) The three dimensions are x + 1 = 5, x + 2 = 6 and x − 2 = 2, so S = 2(5 × 2 + 2 × 6 + 6 × 5) = 2(10 + 12 + 30) = 2(52) = 104 m². (iv) Cost C = 104 × 25 = Rs 2600. (v) 1 m³ can store 1000 litre, so 60 m³ can store 60000 litre.
